domain: Islamic Jurisprudence / Legal Theory / Comparative Law
topic_summary: Analysis of the four Sunni schools of jurisprudence (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali) as a contested kernel where each school reads the same jurisprudential-method commitment differently, grounding interpretive authority through distinct epistemological frameworks while maintaining mutual recognition across centuries without displacement.

key_entities: Hanafi school (rationalist usul al-fiqh; ra'y and qiyas emphasis)
Shafi'i school (systematic hadith hierarchy; rejection of istihsan)
Hanbali school (textualist; minimal qiyas; hadith primacy)
Ijma' (consensus mechanism, differently scoped by schools)
key_tensions: Rationalist vs textualist epistemology (Hanafi/Maliki vs Hanbali)
Hadith hierarchy vs local practice primacy (Shafi'i vs Maliki)
Analogical reasoning scope (broad Hanafi qiyas vs restricted Hanbali qiyas)
Authority grounding: founder's method vs regional continuity vs hadith corpus vs text literalism

axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; distinct authority-grounding via rationalist epistemology

axes.primary_observable: Weight given to 'amal al-Madina in legal rulings; maslaha invocations
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; distinct authority-grounding via geographic/temporal continuity

axes.primary_observable: Hadith authentication requirements in fatawa; rejection rate of istihsan/maslaha arguments
axes.selection_reason: Third reading of contested kernel; distinct authority-grounding via hadith corpus systematization

axes.structural_delta: Jurisprudential method grounded in text literalism and minimal analogical reasoning; authority derives from Ahmad ibn Hanbal's hadith primacy
axes.primary_observable: Qiyas restriction scope; reliance on weak hadith over qiyas
axes.selection_reason: Fourth reading of contested kernel; distinct authority-grounding via text literalism

axes.selection_reason: Independent coordination mechanism; survives §3 test as distinct observable from kernel readings

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Political overlay on kernel structure; captured indirectly via taqlid mechanism's coordination function

omegas.description: Why do Ja'fari and Zaydi schools not participate in the same mutual-recognition structure? Is Sunni/Shi'a split a different kernel or a foreclosure edge?
Does modern Salafism's rejection of taqlid constitute a fifth reading or an attempt to collapse the kernel itself? Authority-grounding via 'direct Quran/Sunnah access' vs madhab mediation.
Each school defines ijma' (consensus) scope differently. Is this a sub-kernel within usul al-fiqh or a downstream coordination mechanism?
Do the four schools converge on gender-related rulings despite methodological differences? If so, is the kernel contested on method but not on substantive outcomes in specific domains?

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel structure confirmed: four readings share usul al-fiqh commitment but ground authority differently. Taqlid mechanism survives §3 as independent coordination axis.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Usul al-fiqh (jurisprudential methodology): the shared commitment to deriving Islamic law from foundational sources (Quran, Sunnah, ijma', qiyas) through systematic interpretive principles
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Each school grounds interpretive legitimacy differently: Hanafi via rationalist framework, Maliki via Medinan continuity, Shafi'i via hadith systematization, Hanbali via text literalism. All claim fidelity to the same kernel while reading it through incompatible epistemological lenses.

readings.authority_grounding: Abu Hanifa's rationalist epistemology; Iraqi scholarly tradition
readings.expected_structural_delta: Broad qiyas scope; istihsan acceptance; rationalist jurists as primary beneficiaries; strict textualists as victims

readings.commitment: Jurisprudential method privileges Medinan customary practice ('amal) and public interest (maslaha mursala) as authoritative sources
readings.authority_grounding: Geographic/temporal continuity with Prophet's city; Malik ibn Anas's Muwatta
readings.expected_structural_delta: Regional practice primacy; maslaha invocations; customary law practitioners as beneficiaries; hadith purists as victims

readings.expected_structural_delta: Hadith corpus primacy; istihsan/maslaha rejection; hadith scholars as beneficiaries; customary practitioners as victims

readings.expected_structural_delta: Qiyas restriction; text literalism; traditionalists as beneficiaries; rationalist interpreters as victims

axiom_contradictions.basis: Hanafi epistemology holds that reason can independently generate legal rulings through qiyas/istihsan; Hanbali epistemology holds that only transmitted text can authorize rulings. No single framework can hold both: accepting reason as independent source requires rejecting text-only constraint, and vice versa.

Maliki epistemology holds that Medinan customary practice ('amal) has independent authority even against isolated hadith; Shafi'i epistemology holds that only authenticated hadith can override other authenticated hadith. No single framework can hold both: accepting 'amal as authoritative requires rejecting hadith-only hierarchy, and vice versa.

Hanafi epistemology accepts istihsan (juristic preference) as a valid source; Shafi'i epistemology categorically rejects istihsan as arbitrary. No single framework can hold both: accepting istihsan as valid requires rejecting its categorical prohibition, and vice versa.
